name: Chip
description: A compact control for a filter option or an entered value that can be selected or removed, such as a filter for "Remote" jobs or a recipient in an email field. For a static category, use a Tag.
summary: Compact control that can be selected or removed
htmlElement: <button> with aria-pressed, or text with a remove <button>

elements.name: Label
elements.description: The option or value, kept short

elements.name: Leading icon
elements.description: Icon, Avatar or check mark before the label

elements.name: Selected state
elements.description: Fill plus a check mark, so the state doesn't depend on color alone

configOptions.options: Filter (toggles on and off), Input (removable value)
None, Icon, Avatar, Check mark when selected

variants.caption: Input — removable values inside a field

usageNotes: A Chip is interactive; a Tag and a Badge are not. If nothing happens when it's pressed, use a Tag.
Build a filter chip as a <button> with aria-pressed, like the APG toggle button. When only one option can be chosen, use a Radio group or Segmented control rather than chips that just look exclusive.
Make the remove control its own <button> with a name that includes the value, such as "Remove Paris". A bare "×" gives screen reader users nothing to go on.
When a chip is removed, move focus to the next chip or back to the input so keyboard users keep their place.
Show the selected state with more than color, such as a check mark plus a change of fill (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color).
